findings.checklist_item: Specify the full `overlap` propagation path to `req.with_inputs` — mirror probe_criteria exactly: a new `overlap` input on the plan-review gate workflow, a `gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict(overlap=...)` parameter wired into run_workflow inputs, a `with: overlap: ${{ inputs.overlap }}` line on the batch finders step, and propagation of the review_plan `overlap` param down through _run_plan_review and the orchestrator into gate_dispatch — not just the review_plan parameter and the req.with_inputs read.

gate_dispatch.py:183 places `probe_criteria` into run_workflow inputs; plan-review.yaml:66 maps `${{ inputs.probe_criteria }}` onto the batch finders step `with:`; only then does production_batch_runner.py:123 read `req.with_inputs.get('probe_criteria')`

review_plan (__init__.py:199-212) has parameters ref/source/repo_root/config/runner/sign/emit_sidecar/advisory_cap/force/retry — no probe_criteria, confirming workflow-input values are NOT review_plan parameters

The chain review_plan -> _run_plan_review -> orchestrator (orchestrator.py:499 gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict) -> gate YAML -> BatchRunRequest is omitted from the plan's description of how `overlap` reaches run_pass1
findings.finding: The `overlap` switch's data flow is incomplete: the plan declares it as a keyword parameter on `review_plan` AND says it 'rides req.with_inputs -- the seam already carrying probe_criteria', but those are two different seams the plan never connects. `probe_criteria` does not reach `req.with_inputs` via a `review_plan` parameter — it is threaded gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict(probe_criteria=...) -> run_workflow inputs -> gate YAML `inputs.probe_criteria` -> the batch step's `with: probe_criteria: ${{ inputs.probe_criteria }}`. `review_plan` has no `probe_criteria` parameter and does not assemble the BatchRunRequest. As written, setting review_plan(overlap=True) would never populate req.with_inputs, so nothing would be injected.
findings.location: Approach, 'On demand, not on every review' paragraph
scenarios: An implementer adds overlap=False to review_plan, confirms AC5 (identity unchanged with overlap=False), but AC1 fails because overlap=True never reaches run_pass1: the value dies at the review_plan boundary and never enters req.with_inputs.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread `overlap` exactly as `probe_criteria` is threaded: add `overlap: bool = False` to review_plan, pass it through _run_plan_review/orchestrator into gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict, place it in the run_workflow inputs dict, declare `overlap` under the gate YAML `inputs:` and add `overlap: ${{ inputs.overlap }}` to the finders batch step `with:`, then read it via req.with_inputs.get('overlap') in ProductionBatchRunner.run and pass to run_pass1.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the overlap advisory finding is attributed so the deterministic decide pass partitions it to `advisory` (e.g. a registered overlap criterion with `default_posture: advisory`, or an explicit decision/posture stamped on the finding), rather than relying solely on the injected prompt's 'never block' directive.
evidence: Plan directive: 'emit one advisory finding per overlapping candidate naming its id and why; emit none when nothing overlaps; never block.'

The finding rides an EXISTING Pass-1 chunk via _chunk_extra_context (pass1.py:215, call-site :326); it is attributed to whatever criteria that chunk already carries, not a dedicated overlap criterion.

block-vs-advisory is assigned deterministically by the decide pass, not by the finder prompt: orchestrator.py:294-301 partitions llm_findings by `decision`, and `_any_blocking_criterion` (orchestrator.py:319) keys the decision on the criterion's registry `default_posture`.

No `overlap` criterion exists in criteria_routing.json (searched: the only 'overlap' hit is unrelated G3/G4 'scope overlap' prose at :878), so there is no advisory-posture criterion for the overlap finding to inherit.

T8 class: a processing/decision rule ('never block') referenced in the injected prompt but not co-located with the schema/mechanism (criterion posture + decide-pass partition) that actually determines the block/advisory outcome.
findings.finding: The injected overlap block's 'never block' decision rule is enforced only by prompt text; the plan does not specify the criterion attribution (criteria[]/default_posture) that makes the downstream deterministic decide pass partition the overlap finding into `advisory` rather than `blocking`.
findings.location: Approach — 'The injected block carries its decision rule' / 'Degradation'; AC 'An overlap finding never changes a review's verdict from pass to block'
scenarios: A plan that genuinely overlaps another ticket is judged inside a Pass-1 chunk carrying a blocking-posture criterion; the overlap finding is attributed there and partitioned to `blocking`, flipping a pass to block despite the directive.
The decide pass drops or mis-buckets the overlap finding because its criteria[]/decision do not resolve to a registered advisory criterion.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the criterion id the overlap finding is emitted under and give it (or stamp the finding with) an advisory posture so orchestrator's posture-keyed partition cannot route it to `blocking`; tie the pass→block AC to that mechanism, not the prompt sentence.

Multiple proving commands (the seeded-store overlap test, the provider-cleared lexical-tier test, the index-absent/catch-up-failed status tests) target symbols and the index the sibling creates. If that work is not yet merged, those tests cannot run.
findings.location: Approach — 'Reuse the index; add no second retrieval path'

findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit `depends_on` edge to the sibling similar-tickets ticket and cite it where find_similar / RESULT_LIMIT are referenced.
